title: Diff Checker: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Diff Checker: Compare two texts line by line — added, removed and unchanged lines highlighted. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example…
content:
The [Diff Checker](/diff-checker) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Compare two texts line by line — added, removed and unchanged lines highlighted. Enter your original text and changed text and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Compare two texts line by line and see exactly what changed: added lines in green, removed lines in red, unchanged lines in grey. It is the same idea as the diff in version control, for any two pieces of text — two drafts of a document, two versions of a config file, or a before-and-after of an edit. The comparison runs entirely in your browser, so the texts never leave your device. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Diff Checker

Start by typing or pasting your original text, then typing or pasting your changed text. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Paste the original text in the left box and the changed text in the right box.
2. Read the highlighted diff — green lines were added, red lines were removed.
3. Copy the diff or swap the two sides to see the change from the other direction.

## How it works

The [Diff Checker](/diff-checker) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. Comparing “The quick brown fox / jumps over the lazy dog” with “The quick brown fox / leaps over the lazy dog” shows one removed line (“jumps…”) and one added line (“leaps…”), with the other lines unchanged. Try the same figures in the [Diff Checker](/diff-checker) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## Trying it out

The fastest way to see what the [Diff Checker](/diff-checker) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## How the diff works

The tool compares the two texts line by line and finds the longest common subsequence — the lines that appear in both, in order. Everything else is an addition (in the new text only) or a removal (in the old text only). A changed line shows as one removal plus one addition, because the tool compares whole lines, not words inside a line.

## What it is good for

Checking what changed between two drafts, spotting accidental edits in a config file, comparing two versions of a document before publishing, or reviewing a student's revision. For code, a proper diff tool in your editor is better — it understands syntax — but for plain text this is the quick check.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- A changed line shows as one removal plus one addition.
- Swap the two sides to read the change in the other direction.
- Very long texts (over 500 lines) are truncated to keep the page fast.

## Frequently asked questions

### What does a diff checker do?

It compares two texts line by line and highlights what changed: added lines, removed lines, and lines that stayed the same. Try it with your own numbers in the [Diff Checker](/diff-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Why does a changed line show as two lines?

The comparison works line by line, so an edited line is one removal (the old wording) plus one addition (the new wording). Try it with your own numbers in the [Diff Checker](/diff-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Can I compare files, not pasted text?

Paste the file contents into the two boxes. The comparison runs in your browser, so the text never leaves your device. Try it with your own numbers in the [Diff Checker](/diff-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is there a size limit?

Each side is limited to 500 lines, so the comparison stays fast. For larger files, use a diff tool in your editor. Try it with your own numbers in the [Diff Checker](/diff-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.
